cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations. Moses says that if Israel faithfully obeys the voice of the LORD their God, He "…will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) Notice that little word "if" leading the way, friends. It's the hinge the whole promise swings on.

The answer is in the city and in the country. Moses says, "You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country." (Deuteronomy 28:3) Downtown or out in the fields, friends, the blessing is there. That's about as wide as a list can get.

The answer is True. Moses says, "The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as well as the produce of your land and the offspring of your livestock—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks." (Deuteronomy 28:4) Children, crops, calves and lambs, all of it gets named. Moses doesn't skip anybody on this list.

The answer is the kneading bowl. Moses says, "Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed." (Deuteronomy 28:5) A kneading bowl is where dough gets worked, friends, so you can guess I felt that one personally. I may have wiped a happy tear off my mustache.

The answer is False. Moses says, "You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out." (Deuteronomy 28:6) No warning, no fine print about leaving, friends. Coming in and going out are both covered.
The word is defeated. Moses says, "The LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against you to be defeated before you." (Deuteronomy 28:7) Notice who does the causing, friends. It's the LORD.

The word is holy. Moses says, "The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in His ways." (Deuteronomy 28:9) That goes deeper than full barns, bakers. It's about who they belong to.

The answer is that they'll stand in awe of Israel. Moses says, "Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) They see the LORD's name on Israel, friends, and awe is what follows.

The word is rain. Moses says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain in season means the right water at the right time, bakers. Any farmer would call that a good day.

The answer is False. Moses says, "You will lend to many nations, but borrow from none." (Deuteronomy 28:12) Lending to many and borrowing from none, friends, that's the promise. The question had the direction backwards.

The answer is the head and not the tail. Moses says, "The LORD will make you the head and not the tail…" (Deuteronomy 28:13) The head leads and the tail follows, friends. That's the picture Moses paints.

The answer is turn aside to the right or the left. Moses says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today…" (Deuteronomy 28:14) Stay on the path, bakers. No wandering off to either side.

The answer is True. Moses finishes the warning with "…and do not go after other gods to serve them." (Deuteronomy 28:14) That's how this part of his speech ends, friends. It goes right back to obeying the LORD alone.
